key_insight: Big Tech's token maxing is textbook Goodhart's Law — measuring AI usage as a KPI produces theater, not productivity. Meanwhile the real story is a quiet massive in-house AI infra buildout, shrinking teams (two-pizza -> one-pizza), and the software engineer role collapsing into 'manager without the bad parts' — a mech suit operator running 7 things at once, getting orchestration + leverage without the people drama.

strategic_context: HIGH. This is the best available field report on what Big Tech is actually doing with AI — the strategic background for every client conversation and architectural decision we make. Specifically validates (1) our tmux-workers-per-developer pattern as equivalent to the Nvidia OpenClaw-K8s pattern, (2) our focus on outcomes-not-metrics aligns with Gergely's Goodhart warning, (3) the 'manager without management' framing is the cleanest public articulation of what our orchestrator actually does for a solo operator, (4) the in-house AI infra buildout means we are competing with internal platform teams (not products), which is a favorable landscape, (5) the Shopify recruitment-investment framing gives us a new angle for German client conversations where recruitment is the real pain.

goodharts_law_warning.rule: Never measure agent usage (token spend, prompts, sessions, minutes) as a KPI
goodharts_law_warning.reason: Meta/Salesforce/Microsoft examples prove the minute AI usage becomes visible, engineers optimize the metric not the outcome
instead_measure: Outcomes shipped (PRs merged, incidents resolved, tests passing)
Rework rate (PRs that need fixing after merge)
goodharts_law_warning.engineer_quote: Instead of reading the docs, I'll ask the agent to summarize and ask questions even if it doesn't do a good job — my count goes up
